description:
We are industrial team—a driven and curious team of pre-industrial engineering students united by creativity, teamwork, and a passion for solving real-world problem

through technology and computing. Our engineering mindset pushes us to tackle tough challenges head-on. Changing climate patterns are making traditional farming increasingly unpredictable. Our mission is to bridge that gap building Agropredict, a user-friendly web decision support tools.
summary:
AgroPredict is a decision-support tool (web application) that helps farmers choose crop rotations adapted to climate change while preserving soil health. Farmers enter their field’s characteristics, such as location, current crop and priorities (yield, water saving, soil regeneration). The tool combines these inputs with NASA Earth observation data, including soil moisture, precipitation, temperature and vegetation indices, to assess local climate risks like drought, heavy rainfall and heat stress. Based on this analysis, it recommends suitable crops and rotation sequences, for example alternating cereals with nitrogen-fixing legumes to restore the soil. Results are displayed on a results dashboard, simple recommendations.
The tool addresses the Field Shift challenge by turning complex satellite data into actionable advice that farmers can use without technical expertise. It matters because climate variability threatens food security, and better rotation choices can stabilize yields, reduce input costs, protect soils over the long term and help communities adapt.
details:
What does AgroPredict do and how does it work?

AgroPredict is a web application that recommends crop rotations adapted to local climate and soil conditions. To do this, the farmer enters their location, current crop, soil characteristics and priorities (yield, water saving, soil regeneration). AgroPredict retrieves the data provided by NASA (soil moisture, precipitation, temperature, vegetation indices) for that location.

A decision logic assesses local climate risks (drought, heavy rainfall, heat stress) as well as the compatibility of each crop with the soil and climate. It then proposes suitable crops and rotation sequences and displays them with clear, simple recommendations.

Benefits

  • It turns complex satellite data into simple advice that can be used without technical expertise.
  • It helps stabilize yields despite climate variability.
  • It reduces input costs (fertilizer, water) and protects soil health in the long term.
  • It makes planning easier before each planting season.

Intended impact of the project: AgroPredict’s overall impact is to make space technology accessible to all farmers so they can protect their harvests from climate disruption.

Tools used

AgroPredict uses NASA Earth observation data (NASA POWER for temperature and precipitation, GPM IMERG for rainfall, SMAP for soil moisture, MODIS/VIIRS for vegetation indices, and ECOSTRESS/HLS for plant water stress), complemented by data from partner agencies such as ESA. The data is retrieved and processed with Python and includes an interactive map (Leaflet and OpenStreetMap).

Where did we use AI

We use AI like :

Google Stich to design the interface

Antigravity to debug

Google AI studio to do audio voice.

How is our project creative?

  • It combines Earth observation data, soil characteristics and the farmer’s priorities in a single tool, instead of giving generic advice.
  • It focuses on rotation sequences over several seasons, not just the choice of one crop.
  • It is designed for non-experts, with a simple interface and clear recommendations.

What factors did our team consider?

  • Climate risks: drought, heavy rainfall and heat stress.
  • Soil structure and soil health, including nitrogen restoration through legumes.
  • Data availability: only the data provided by the organizers.
  • Ease of use for farmers with limited technical knowledge and limited internet access.
  • Scalability: the logic can be adapted to other regions and other crops.
